It makes no network request, spawns nothing and reads no environment variable. In the default `check` mode it also reads the two output paths and writes no file. Only when the consumer passes `write: true` (mode `write`) does it create the output paths' directories and write the two documents, and nothing else; the consumer chooses both paths. exceptions.justification: The `quickStart` preset (src/presets/quick-start.ts) runs this package's own bin as `repo-contract quick-start --json --readme <file> --timeout <ms>`. It reads that Markdown file and package.json, then runs `npm pack --ignore-scripts` into a temporary directory. It writes a package.json into an empty project beside the tarball and runs each command of the README's marked block there in a shell. The commands are the consumer's own README text. An install among them reaches the configured registry, as it does for any user who copies them. Nothing is sent anywhere by repo-contract itself; the report goes to stdout and the temporary directory is removed. The `mutation` preset (src/presets/mutation.ts) runs `repo-contract mutation run --json` with its options as flags. It deletes only its own files inside the project: Stryker's incremental file, its previous report and its temp dir. It refuses any of the three that resolves outside the project, symbolic links included, and then deletes nothing. On Vitest 5 it patches the test-name separator in `node_modules/@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` (stryker-js#6210), unless `patchVitestRunner: false` passes `--no-patch-vitest-runner`. It then runs the consumer's installed `stryker run <config> --force`, and re-runs at most `--confirm-timeouts` timed-out mutants alone. With the cache on it also runs `git ls-files` and reads the listed files to key the cache under `.repo-contract/cache`. Stryker runs the consumer's own tests; repo-contract sends nothing anywhere. The `npmScript` preset (src/presets/npm-script.ts) runs `repo-contract npm-script <script> --json`, which runs `npm run <script>` from the consumer's own package.json and hashes any `--must-not-change` path before and after.
